themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Accumulation Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints spiked to 4 THIS WEEK, a 357% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 0.9 per week, suggesting a potential public health or sanitation breakdown in CD 209.
evidence: 4 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.21)
Represents 357% spike from baseline, classified as high severity
Aligns with community board priority on public health issues (repeated budget request)
reporting_angles: Interview DSNY about whether there's a disposal backlog, rodent outbreak, or wildlife management issue in Parkchester/Soundview
Check if dead animals are concentrated in specific neighborhoods (parks, commercial areas, residential blocks) to identify root cause

themes_detail.label: Lot Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Lot condition complaints exploded to 3 three weeks ago, a 1100% spike above the 8-week baseline of 0.2 per week, indicating possible widespread property neglect or illegal dumping across the district.
evidence: 3 lot condition complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.35, highest severity)
1100% increase from baseline, highest percentage spike in dataset
Suggests concentrated problem affecting multiple properties or one large vacant lot
reporting_angles: Identify which specific lots are generating complaints via 311 geocoding; visit and photograph them
Cross-reference with DOB permits and ULURP applications (1160 Pugsley Avenue rezoning is in public review) to see if development delays are causing visible blight

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting & Obstruction Wave
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints surged 1100% to 6 last week (vs. 0.5 baseline) and street obstruction complaints jumped 191% to 8 last week (vs. 2.8 baseline), suggesting coordinated illegal activity or infrastructure neglect.
evidence: Illegal posting: 6 complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 4.16, 1100% spike)
Obstruction: 8 complaints last week vs. 2.8 weekly average (z-score: 4.82, 191% spike)
Two parallel spikes last week suggest interconnected street management failure
reporting_angles: Determine whether illegal postings are gang tags, commercial advertising, or political; photograph visible examples along major corridors
Check if obstructions are vendor encroachments, abandoned vehicles, or debris; assess whether Parks or Sanitation enforcement is responding

themes_detail.label: Derelict Vehicles Piling Up
themes_detail.summary: Derelict vehicle complaints reached 34 two weeks ago, a 216% spike above the 8-week baseline of 10.8 per week, indicating abandoned cars are not being removed from streets or lots.
evidence: 34 derelict vehicle complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 10.8 weekly average (z-score: 3.52, 216% spike)
Sustained elevation suggests NYPD tow operations are not keeping pace with abandonment rate
Overlaps with long-standing community concern (illegal parking is 3rd-highest 90-day complaint type at 2,094 total)
reporting_angles: Ride along with NYPD or DOT to document how long abandoned cars remain on streets before removal; measure response time
Interview residents on specific blocks with visible derelict vehicles about impact on quality of life and parking availability

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Disruption
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints spiked to 56 three weeks ago, a 213% increase over the 8-week baseline of 17.9 per week, suggesting new commercial activity, construction, or venues generating disturbance.
evidence: 56 commercial noise complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 17.9 weekly average (z-score: 3.79, 213% spike)
Residential noise (2,456 complaints over 90 days) remains endemic; commercial spike suggests new pressure point
Aligns with 396 total DOB permit filings in past 90 days (293 alterations, 48 new buildings)
reporting_angles: Identify which commercial establishments or construction sites generated the spike; interview neighbors about specific noise types and hours
Cross-reference with DOB permits to determine if new businesses or renovations are operating without proper soundproofing or during restricted hours
